what_happened.line: The Finance and School Committees met jointly and heard a Chapter 70 explainer covering the foundation budget, the required local contribution, circuit breaker and Monty Tech assessments.
The explainer said Chapter 70 foundation aid is less than last year's, so hold harmless and a minimum per-pupil increase make up the difference.
The Finance Committee agreed that the November 4 public hearing will take the TC Passios articles in one combined presentation, with discussion able to cross articles.
The committee set the December 9 agenda: a Chapter 70 follow-up with legislators, ARPA, and Green Communities and streetlights.
Committee reports raised a master plan funding request and a dispute with the utility over the quoted streetlight purchase cost, which the DPU may be asked to settle.

why_it_matters: Chapter 70 state aid is a large share of the school appropriation, and the minimum increase and hold harmless rules set how much of the school budget the town's tax levy has to cover.
The November 4 hearing on the TC Passios articles comes before a special town meeting on November 16, where residents may be asked to vote on those articles.

Most time went to the three TC Passios building articles, where comparison data is late and the design article has no funding source. It also discussed budget priorities and earmarks, approved two sets of minutes, and adjourned.

reconciliation.what: Our minutes against the minutes the town published. caption_error = the same fact the captions rendered badly, resolved by the official reading shown beside the as-heard one; discrepancy = a substantive difference, flagged and not resolved. Neither record is treated as the referee.
reconciliation.summary: Neither record has a vote, and the two agree on free cash ($2,665,798) and the 38 percent salt increase. They differ on what was discussed: our minutes carry two transfers and several figures the official minutes omit, and the official minutes carry the Nov 4 hearing and Oct 28 joint meeting that ours omit. A reader should check who the Town Manager was, because ours names "Adam" as town manager and Heather as finance director, while the official minutes name Heather Lemieux as Town Manager.

what_happened.line: The Finance Committee took no formal position on the TC Passios building articles but leaned toward deferring articles K and L.
The committee walked through the special town meeting warrant, asking the town manager for amounts and short write-ups on each article.
Article L, the design article, needs funding but has no source named; free cash is the likely one.
The chair plans to hear the TC Passios articles in order next week, decide then, and invite building committee leadership.
No votes were taken on articles; the committee approved two sets of minutes and adjourned.

why_it_matters: The TC Passios articles would ask Town Meeting to spend on a building and its design, and the committee's recommendation on whether to defer them is still unsettled.
If design money for Article L is drawn from free cash, it comes from the town's one-time reserve rather than from the tax levy.
watch_next: The committee's meeting next week, when the chair intends to take up the TC Passios articles in order and decide, with building committee leadership invited.
The amounts for the Article A budget amendment (assistant accountant and IT transfers), due from the town manager next week.
